Description: Husband-and-wife team Fik and Reka Saleh built Fikscue from a pandemic side hustle. Fik is a self-taught pitmaster who started selling brisket on Instagram in June 2020 after losing his day job. Reka, who ran the Indonesian pop-up Gurih Table, turns the smoked trimmings into Indonesian dishes. Their tiny Park Street storefront opened in November 2023. In 2024 the New York Times put it on its list of America's 50 best restaurants, as one of five newly opened California picks. Almond-wood-smoked brisket, dino beef ribs and links share trays with nasi goreng, peanut-sauce slaw and sambal. All meat is halal and there's no pork. Service is counter-only and first-come, first-served, with weekend lines down the block. There's courtyard seating, or you can eat at the brewery next door if you buy a drink.
Verify Before Publishing: Hours need checking. KQED (2024) reported Saturday–Sunday, noon–4pm, but hours may have expanded. Also has a Thrive City (San Francisco) location; confirm owners are comfortable with an 'independent' label.

Address: 1332 Park Street, Suite D, Alameda, CA 94501
Description: Three San Francisco fine-dining veterans who met at Waterbar opened Alley & Vine in December 2020, at the height of the pandemic. They are beverage director Francisco Bazo (an Alameda resident), Casey Hunt and chef Jason Ryczek, formerly executive chef at Farallon. It sits down an ivy-draped alley off Park Street, with a soaring dining room, a dramatic bar and an open kitchen. Much of the produce and eggs come from Hunt's family farm. Ryczek harvests the house white sturgeon caviar himself at a Central Valley farm and serves it on a biscuit. The seasonal menu changes often, with dishes like Dungeness crab and short rib. It also has one of Alameda's biggest wine lists, a large patio and brunch.
Verify Before Publishing: Yelp lists hours as daily 11am–9pm; confirm current lunch and brunch service.

Description: Asena has been a downtown fixture since 1996. It is owned and run day to day by Mustafa Yildirim and Muhittin Arpaci, who both grew up in Turkey in kitchens where their mothers cured olives and baked bread. The restaurant carries on that from-scratch approach: house-baked bread, hand-rolled pasta, cured salmon and preserved lemons. Seasonal Cal-Med menus use local and organic produce and always include gluten-free and vegetarian options. Longtime diners call it an upscale bistro and credit it with raising the bar for Alameda dining. It's a dinner-only spot with reservations, a deep list of small-label wines and a boutique cocktail bar. The owners have also given generously to local schools and charities.
Verify Before Publishing: Owners' combined experience conflicts (official site: 60+ years; Yelp: 30+). Friday–Saturday closing time differs (10pm official, 9:30pm Yelp). Official site says closed Sundays.

Address: 1650 Park Street, Unit A, Alameda, CA 94501
Description: Chef Paul Manousos, who once worked the counter at Farmstead Cheeses & Wines, and Michele Manousos started East End Pizza Co. as a walk-up stall in a back corner of the Alameda Marketplace, with an imported Mugnaini wood-fired oven. On June 4, 2013, they opened a full restaurant next door, with a quartz bar and back-bar boards reclaimed from an old Alameda boathouse. Native-yeast sourdough pizzas come out of the 900-degree oven. Other highlights include oysters shucked to order, house charcuterie, a deboned wood-oven chicken featured in the East Bay Cooks cookbook, and seasonal cocktails. It's open nightly, with weekday happy hours from 5–6pm and 9–10pm, plus takeout, delivery and free parking.
Verify Before Publishing: Founding year conflicts (Alameda Magazine: stall launched spring 2010; East End's site: 'since 2011'). Confirm current hours.

Description: Named for the river that links Laos, Thailand and Vietnam, Mekong Kitchen is a family-run restaurant at the north end of Park Street. It serves dishes from across the region, and diners especially praise its Lao cooking. Regulars order the whole fried tilapia, Lao sausage, basil fried rice, popcorn chicken, grilled chicken and egg rolls. The restaurant says it uses fresh, locally sourced ingredients. The modern, cozy dining room suits a quick lunch or a celebration, and reviewers mention a warm staff who explain the dishes. It serves lunch and dinner with a mid-afternoon break, and offers takeout, delivery and catering.
Verify Before Publishing: Hours conflict (Instagram: closed Thursdays, split service; website: continuous hours). Owner names not published (contact email suggests the Phannavong family, unconfirmed). Founding year not found.

Description: Taco Fino is a true family business. Arcelio and Antonia Serrano left the furniture trade to launch a food truck in January 2023, mostly serving golfers at Buchanan Fields in Concord. They then opened this Park Street storefront, adding 'Express' to tell it apart from the truck. Their youngest son often works the register, and another son, Erik, hand-built the replica of the Park Street Bridge that anchors the dining room. The bestseller is the California burrito, made with tater tots instead of fries. Birria tacos, street tacos, loaded 'Fino Fries,' bowls and nachos round out the menu. It offers counter service, takeout, delivery and catering.
Verify Before Publishing: Address differs: 1506 Park (Yelp, DoorDash) vs 1508 Park (official contact page). Opening date conflicts (site says September 2023; Alameda Post's January 2025 story implies later). Phone is a 925 number.

Restaurant: Toomie's Thai (Toomie's by Thai Golden Rice)
Description: Toomie's has served traditional Thai cooking on Park Street since 2003. The name comes from the nickname of an original co-owner. Alameda Magazine readers voted it the island's best Thai in 2008, and the SF Chronicle praised its curries and seafood. House specials include string beans stir-fried in butter with Thai aromatics and spicy basil duck. Pad thai, pad see ew and spicy fried rice are the regulars' standbys, and the kitchen's 'spicy' is genuinely spicy. It's a casual dining room with good-value lunch specials that come with rice and soup. It's open daily for lunch and dinner, takes reservations and offers takeout, delivery and catering.
Verify Before Publishing: Ownership unclear. Now branded 'Toomie's by Thai Golden Rice'; a separate ordering site uses 'Toomie's Thai by Mee Choke' with phone (510) 865-8011. OpenTable lists Aroon Srisombat as executive chef. An older Patch story (original owners cited for wage violations) predates current branding. Confirm current owner and name.

Cuisine: Pizza (Chicago-style deep dish and thin crust)
Description: Little Star Pizza founders Susannah Blumenstock and Ben Seabury brought their cult-favorite deep dish to Alameda. They took over a historic Park Street building, originally built in 1880 and expanded in 1920, after the previous tenant, Capone's, closed. The signature cornmeal-crust deep-dish pies and thin-crust pizzas come with sandwiches, salads, wings and roasted broccolini. The bar leans on beer and spirits from the island's many breweries and distilleries. The grand, flexible dining room makes it a popular pick for group dinners, private parties and catered events. It's open daily for lunch and dinner, with happy hour, takeout and delivery.
Verify Before Publishing: Part of a small Bay Area group (Little Star/The Star Pizza, with San Francisco and Albany locations). Locally owned but not single-location; editor should decide whether it fits. Instagram now points to group accounts.

Description: Owner Christos Frangoulis opened The Park Street Tavern in 2018 as a casual fine-dining restaurant and bar at the east end of the downtown strip. The menu draws on Greek, Italian and wider Mediterranean traditions. The kitchen is notable for cooking without seed oils. Favorites include chicken piccata, hanger steak, calamari and a house-made cheesecake. It's a relaxed, grown-up spot for date nights and dinner with friends, with a full bar and a neighborhood-tavern feel.
Verify Before Publishing: Confirm current hours, service style (lunch vs dinner only) and reservations. Sources mainly Yelp and the restaurant's own site; little press coverage.

Description: Yellowtail is a long-running, owner-operated sushi bistro in Redwood Square, the courtyard it shares with Alley & Vine. Owners Gary and Joe were profiled in a Patch business spotlight. Diners come for creative specialty rolls like the Cherry Blossom and the Sumo, plus clean, simple nigiri such as hamachi, the fish the restaurant is named after. The full menu also covers cooked Japanese staples. It's a casual, friendly room that works for a weeknight sushi fix, with dine-in, takeout and delivery.
Verify Before Publishing: Only owners' first names found. Founding year not found. Website has changed (yellowtailca.com, yellowtailalameda.com, yellowtailjapanesebistro.com); confirm current site and hours.

Description: Co-owners Donald Kubisch and Amy Griffith are former Alameda residents who met in a San Leandro softball league. They built a following with their food truck, Locos Only, at weekend pop-ups at Alameda Point before taking over the storybook cottage that housed Little House Cafe until 2022. Now painted sunshine yellow with turquoise trim and a giant wooden shaka out front, it serves Hawaiian comfort food in famously massive portions. Order loco moco, lava chicken plates, musubi, malasadas, taro French toast, ube lattes, or shave ice with ice cream. It's counter or QR-code ordering, open 8:30am–3pm and closed Wednesdays.
Verify Before Publishing: Confirm current hours and opening year (2024, per Alameda Post article date).

Address: 2651 Blanding Avenue, Suite E, Alameda, CA 94501
Description: Bacogai means 'three ladies' in Vietnamese, a nod to the women who own it. It sits in the Bridgeside Center overlooking the Tidal Canal. The draw is Vietnamese hot pot (lẩu) built on a rich pork bone-marrow broth, meant for groups who cook meats, seafood and vegetables at the table. Bánh hỏi (delicate woven rice-noodle bundles) with lemongrass pork is another highlight. East Bay Express called it a hotpot hotspot, and The Infatuation has reviewed it too. It's a sit-down dinner spot for families and friends, and took part in Alameda Restaurant Week 2025 and 2026 with a prix-fixe menu.
Verify Before Publishing: Owners' full names not captured (East Bay Express quotes owners surnamed Bui and Tran). Founding year and current hours not confirmed.

Description: Chef-owner Hanh Nguyen has run this tucked-away neighborhood noodle shop just off the main drag since 2013. The name says it all: it's a side-street secret locals send friends to. The kitchen's pride is its broth, simmered 24 to 30 hours with bone marrow. The standout bowl is oxtail pho. Crisp bánh xèo (turmeric rice crêpes) and other Vietnamese classics fill out the menu, and there's a good beer selection. It's a casual, affordable spot for lunch or dinner, with dine-in and takeout.
Verify Before Publishing: Yelp shows two phone numbers, (510) 808-5298 and (341) 220-9041; confirm which is current. Hours not confirmed.

Description: Marti's Place is a small, owner-run breakfast and lunch spot in the Chestnut Station building on Encinal Avenue. Owner Marti is a familiar face to regulars, and the place has been serving Alameda since at least the 2000s. The menu mixes diner comfort with a few surprises. The Swedish pancakes with lingonberry are the signature, alongside chilaquiles and the house special omelet. It's a cozy, no-frills neighborhood café where locals linger over coffee.
Verify Before Publishing: No official website. Only owner's first name known; founding year not found. Yelp listing last updated May 2026; call to confirm still open and current hours.

Description: Acapulco is one of Alameda's oldest restaurants. It was founded in 1953 by Modesto and Rose Quintero at the corner of Lincoln and Willow. In late 2011, restaurateurs Michael Wiesner (of Paradiso and Boulevard Burger) and Gordon Galvan bought it, and they reopened it after a renovation in August 2013. The menu sticks to its Mexican-American roots. Regulars order chile relleno, chile verde, chile colorado and the house Acapulco taco, often with margaritas. It's a family-friendly sit-down spot with a bar.
Verify Before Publishing: Current (2026) ownership not confirmed; Wiesner/Galvan ownership dates to 2011–2013. Apple Maps lists it as 'Acapulco Nuevo'; confirm preferred name and hours.

Description: Ceron Kitchen fulfills a lifelong dream for Vicente Ceron, who built several successful construction companies before partnering with his friend, executive chef Juan Jaquez. Jaquez previously cooked at San Leandro's Paradiso and San Francisco's Boulevard. The SF Chronicle called it an unusually splashy arrival for Webster Street, and Eater SF listed it as an East Bay hot spot. Jaquez's menu includes octopus a la plancha with Spanish chorizo and beans, steak with carrot-top chimichurri, pork belly tostadas, seafood pasta, and duck with risotto. Cocktails are a highlight. It serves lunch, dinner and weekend brunch, with OpenTable reservations, a chef's table, a private room, a patio and a parking lot.
Verify Before Publishing: Owner's first name spelled 'Vincente' (SF Chronicle) vs 'Vicente' (official site). Opened early 2022 in former Otaez space. Instagram hours: Fri–Sat 11am–10pm, Sun–Thu 11am–9pm.

Description: Chef-owner Saboor Zafari has cooked for Alameda for more than 25 years. He opened Angela's in the Marina Village Shopping Center in 2001, then moved to Oak and Central, then to Park Street near the Marketplace. On August 4, 2026, he reopened in the former Yokohama sushi space on Webster, Angela's fourth Alameda home. The menu blends the Afghan dishes Zafari grew up with, Mediterranean braises and grills, and organic Northern California produce. Longtime signatures include duck strudel with cranberry wine sauce, leek-and-spinach bolani, Afghan pasta pockets with saffron yogurt, and house chutneys. It's a small, cooked-to-order kitchen that handles custom requests. Reservations are available online.
Verify Before Publishing: Service hours conflict (Nosh: lunch and dinner after soft opening; website: dinner only, Tue–Sun 5–9pm). Old 1640 Park Street listing (Angela's Kitchen) is closed; don't use it.

Description: Owner Constanza Ortiz named her takeout counter after Macondo, the mythical town in Gabriel García Márquez's novels. Since opening in 2022, she has paired handmade Colombian empanadas and buñuelos with fusion arepas that start from a classic cheese arepa and pick up flavors from around the world. Weekend specials like frijolada Colombiana and sides of baked plantains and Colombian-style beans nod to home cooking. East Bay Express called it part of Webster Street's reawakening. It's a takeout and catering spot rather than a sit-down restaurant, open Wednesday–Sunday, 10am–3pm per East Bay Express.
Verify Before Publishing: Hours from East Bay Express may have changed. One aggregator calls it a 'food truck,' but it's a storefront counter.

Description: A family with roots in Ensenada, Baja California, has run Calafia on Webster since June 2003. It's a West End staple known for fresh food, cold beer and a laid-back back patio next to Webster Park's public art. Tamales and chiles rellenos are made daily. The al pastor burrito is a local favorite, and Baja-style fish tacos, enchiladas and a taco bar round things out. Taco Tuesdays pack the place, and the family also caters around the island. During Alameda Restaurant Week 2026, a free fish taco offer drew crowds. It offers counter service, dine-in, takeout and catering.
Verify Before Publishing: Owners' full names not confirmed (website calls it 'Macri's dream'; contact email is victor@). Confirm hours.

Description: Chef-owner Joann Guitarte and her partner Bobeck Parandian, formerly of Bowzer's Pizza, opened Cafe Jolie in 2012 in the old Tillie's Diner space and named it after their daughter. It has become one of the West End's go-to brunch spots, with a French accent. Order the beignets with chocolate sauce for the table, then crab cake Benedict, croque monsieur or steak frites. Alameda Post named it among the island's brunch spots worth your weekend plans. It's a casual, cheerful room for breakfast and lunch, with dine-in and takeout. The same owners run Cafe Jolie Petit on Bay Farm and Donut Petit nearby.
Verify Before Publishing: Confirm current hours.

Neighborhood: West End (Santa Clara Avenue at Webster)
Description: Donut Petit is the doughnut shop from the Cafe Jolie team. Co-owner Joann Guitarte makes the doughnuts herself, starting at 4 every morning according to East Bay Express. It opened in March 2020 with a grand opening on March 28. The case holds classic and creative raised and cake doughnuts, mochi doughnuts and cronuts. The salted-caramel old-fashioned with pecans and Himalayan salt is a signature. For something savory, the 'Donut Monsieur' puts a croque-monsieur between doughnut halves. It's a grab-and-go morning stop with a few seats.
Verify Before Publishing: No standalone website confirmed. Confirm hours.

Description: East Ocean started in Oakland Chinatown in the 1980s under the Low family and has anchored Webster Street since 1995. Its big banquet halls fill for weekend dim sum, weddings and family celebrations. By day, carts and menus offer har gow, siu mai and baked custard buns. At night, the kitchen turns to Cantonese seafood, and its smoked black cod is famous. East Bay Express profiled its dim sum-by-day, smoked cod-by-night rhythm. It's a large, lively, family-friendly room that's good for groups, with dine-in and takeout.
Verify Before Publishing: Ownership unclear: founded by the Low family, but a review says it was sold; a manager named David says on Yelp it's the 'same team.' Founding year 1983 (East Bay Express) vs 1985 (Instagram). Now also has a Walnut Creek location.

Description: 1400 Bar & Grill is in the historic Croll Building at the corner of Webster and Central, one of the West End's oldest commercial landmarks. It's a friendly neighborhood bar and grill serving hearty pub classics. Burgers, including a poblano burger, are the main draw, along with wings, pizza and a cult-favorite side of Spam fries. Reviewers mention hosts Yanni and Michael and a Sunday special from Chef Fernando. It's a casual spot for game days, happy hour and group dinners, with a full bar, and it's listed on OpenTable.
Verify Before Publishing: Ownership not confirmed (contact email suggests the Cooperakis family). Founding year not found. Yelp lists a different website (1400barandgrill.com). Ask the owner for a blurb.

Description: India Palace has been one of Alameda's go-to Indian restaurants for more than three decades, in business since the early 1990s. Owner Kulbir personally answers guest reviews online. The lunch buffet is a longtime West End habit, and at dinner the menu covers North Indian standards, led by chicken tikka masala and lamb palak, plus tandoori dishes, curries and fresh naan. It's a comfortable, family-run dining room on Buena Vista just off Webster, with dine-in, takeout and delivery.
Verify Before Publishing: Founding year conflicts (Yelp 1991, Facebook 1992). Only owner's first name known. Confirm buffet days and hours.

Neighborhood: West End (Main Street, near Alameda Point)
Description: Share Pizza's founder Victor is an alum of the Arizmendi worker-owned bakery cooperative. He named the business after his wife Sharon's nickname, 'Share.' He launched it in August 2020 as a half-bake pizza delivery service during the pandemic, and it has since grown into a storefront kitchen. Pies are built on a naturally leavened sourdough crust with seasonal toppings. Favorites include the 'United We Stand' combo and a mushroom pie. Half-baked pizzas to finish at home are still a specialty. It offers takeout, delivery and half-bake orders.
Verify Before Publishing: Has moved: older listings (incl. Restaurant Week) place it at Alameda Point; now at 1930 Main Street. Only owner's first name known. Confirm hours.

Description: The Rake is the pub attached to Admiral Maltings, a craft malthouse that has been floor-malting California-grown barley at Alameda Point since August 2017. The pub opened in January 2018. Windows look onto the malting floor, and the ever-changing tap list features beers from regional brewers who use Admiral's malt. The food is honest pub fare: bratwurst, soft pretzels, pulled pork and tri-tip plates, cured meats, cheese and sandwiches, with vegetarian and vegan options. It has a warm, rustic vibe, a deck, free board games, and it welcomes kids and dogs. It's open daily from midday, with events and private parties.
Verify Before Publishing: Owners' and founders' names not found. Yelp hours: Mon 12–7pm, Tue–Thu 12–8pm, Fri 12–9pm, Sat 11:30am–9pm, Sun 11:30am–7pm.

Description: Firebrand started in Oakland in 2008. It moved its bakery and a new café into a converted naval warehouse at Alameda Point, fired by a wood-burning Llopis oven. Led by CEO Matt Kreutz, the company is known for a mission-driven hiring model that gives jobs to people who were formerly incarcerated or homeless. The café sells the sourdough and levain loaves that supply many Bay Area restaurants, plus bombolini, pastries, sandwiches, and drinks like an ube latte. The airy industrial space is a weekend destination for Alameda Point visitors.
Verify Before Publishing: Café opened June 2023 next to a production facility that opened the year before. SF Chronicle reports the City lent $300,000 to finish the café. Yelp describes it as employee-owned; confirm. Confirm café hours.

Address: 800 West Tower Avenue (inside SoFive Soccer Center / The Hub), Alameda, CA 94501
Description: C'era Una Volta ('once upon a time') was founded by Italians with roots in Palermo and Livorno and for years was a sit-down Alameda favorite. Chef Rutilio 'Rudy' Fanetti-Duran is one of only a handful of Bay Area chefs recognized by L'Associazione Cuochi Fiorentini, and the restaurant earned recognition from the Accademia Italiana della Cucina. Today it runs mostly as a kitchen and catering operation, offering weekly three-entrée meal packages, chef's specials for two or four, and party trays. Dishes range from truffle gnocchi and artichoke ravioli to a Tuscan mixed grill, with vegan options. It offers pickup, local delivery and catering (48 hours' notice).
Verify Before Publishing: Address conflicts: official site lists 800 W. Tower Ave (SoFive/Bladium); Downtown Alameda directory lists 2534 Santa Clara Ave ('at Flavor Island'); Facebook says 'now in Alameda's Spirits Alley.' Confirm whether any dine-in.

Description: The Bay Farm offshoot of Cafe Jolie opened in 2023. Owners Joann Guitarte and Bobeck Parandian run it out of a shipping-container café in the Harbor Bay business park. It brings a slightly shorter version of the Webster Street brunch menu to the south side of the island, beignets included, along with egg dishes, sandwiches and coffee. Seating is mostly outdoors, which makes it a sunny-day favorite for office workers, cyclists on the Bay Trail and families.
Verify Before Publishing: Mostly outdoor seating, so hours may change with weather. Restaurant Week spells it 'Petite'; business uses 'Petit'.

Address: 891 Island Drive, Suite A, Alameda, CA 94502
Description: China Villa is a long-standing neighborhood Chinese restaurant in the Harbor Bay Landing center on Bay Farm Island, with views over the lagoon. It's one of the few sit-down dinner options on the south side of the island. Regulars order the house China Villa Chicken, walnut fish and Mongolian beef, along with the usual Chinese-American favorites. It's a relaxed, family-friendly dining room, busy with takeout.
Verify Before Publishing: Owners unknown (a Foursquare tip mentions an ownership change around 2014). Founding year not found. October 2025 preliminary plans to redevelop Harbor Bay Landing into 300+ homes (proposal only). Call to confirm hours.

Description: Mosley's sits at the end of the Grand Marina pier, surrounded by sailboats. Cristin Shea founded it in 2015 and named it after her dog, Mosley. Chef-owner Scott Cordie took over on June 2, 2020, and has kept its regulars-first spirit. The kitchen bakes its own scones and pastries. For lunch, it serves sandwiches like a well-loved tuna melt, and its charcuterie boxes are good for a picnic on the docks. Cordie also teaches charcuterie classes. It's a small, dog-friendly waterfront café for breakfast and lunch, with patio seating.
Verify Before Publishing: One blog calls the chef 'Scott Mosley,' which appears wrong; use Scott Cordie. Confirm hours.
